newsitem.title: USA: Canadian Natural sees growth from drilling.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Natural sees growth from drilling.

text.p: Canadian Natural Resources Ltd, fresh from its C$654-million takeover of Sceptre Resources, is expected to post major production and financial increases this year and next without more acquisitions, company chairman Allan Markin said on Thursday.

Markin told an investment symposium sponsored by FirstEnergy Capital Corp and Merrill Lynch & Co that his firm's oil and natural gas liquids output should balloon to 62,500 barrels per day in 1997, up from an estimated average of 36,000 barrels per day in 1996.
Gas production is expected to jump to 625 million cubic feet per day in 1997, up from an estimated 500 million cubic feet per day this year, he said.
Most of the growth was expected to be achieved through drilling in western Canada, which will see a major surge over the next few years, Markin said.
Canadian Natural, whose share price has soared in 1996, set its 1997 drilling target at 700 wells, up from an expected 400 this year, he said. Just under 1,000 could be drilled in 1998, he said.
The activity will play a big part of 1997 capital expenditures, which were forecast at C$700 million, up from about C$525 million in 1996, Markin said.
While Canadian Natural was "pleasantly surprised" with several of the assets it acquired in the Sceptre takeover, the company has no plans for more corporate acquisitions, Markin said.

"From an acquisition standpoint for corporations, the answer is no," he said. "The only reason we did Sceptre is that we were one of two or three companies that their board of directors actually pursued to buy it."
Markin said Canadian Natural was poised to post 1996 cash flow of C$350 million -- a C$15-million increase from previous estimates -- and 1997 cash flow of C$475 million, or C$4.83 per share.
However, if oil prices in 1997 averaged US$20 per barrel, cash flow could hit C$500 million, he said.
Markin said the company's production mix was expected to hit 50-50 oil and gas in 1997.
